source_text: As President Donald Trump’s approval rating plunges to a historic low of 36 percent, experts have an increasingly dismal assessment of his second administration. “This is what a crater looks like in politics,” said pollster and political analyst Cornell Belcher . “By every key objective measure this is clearly a failed presidency.” Trump’s approval rating was already low, but his latest drop is among the sharpest declines of either of his terms. It comes as he confronts a series of crises largely of his own making. The first is the economy. In 2024, voters overwhelmingly ranked the economy as their top concern — its strongest influence since the Great Recession of 2008. Cost of living skyrocketed in the wake of COVID-19, and while then-President Joe Biden’s administration reduced inflation and rebounded the economy faster than any other nation , a financially rattled electorate voted for Trump thinking his economic approach would outperform that of Kamala Harris, who was widely viewed as a continuation of Biden. But voter hopes haven’t panned out. Today, only 29 percent of Americans approve of Trump’s economic stewardship, while just 25 percent approve of his handling of the cost of living. “It’s important that people know that the president feels their pain and that help is on the way,” said Amanda Makki, a Republican political strategist and lawyer. Trump hasn’t exactly delivered on that, famously making obtuse statements like “maybe the children will have 2 dolls instead of 30 ” as the economy soured under the weight of his tariffs. What’s more, the fact that gas prices are approaching record highs not only says something about the Trump economy, but links to the second major reason Americans are displeased with the president: his war on Iran. Just 35 percent of Americans approve of Trump’s actions in Iran, down from 37 percent a week ago. Only 26 percent agree with Trump’s assertion that the war will make the U.S. safer, and a mere 7 percent support his suggestion of putting boots on the ground. And with gas prices spiking up to a national average just shy of $4 and no clear end in sight to the war, Americans are not happy with how Trump’s military “excursion” is hurting them at the pump. Trump may dismiss concerns over affordability as a “Democratic hoax,” but voters aren’t buying it.

source_text:
Golden Village has announced that its Tiong Bahru Plaza outlet will close at the end of March 2026 after more than 30 years in operation, making it one of the oldest cinemas in Singapore to shut in recent years. The official explanation points to streaming platforms and changing audience habits. But as theatres steadily disappear, that explanation may serve to distract from a larger question: who benefits when shared public spaces are replaced by more controlled ways of consuming entertainment?

The closures include Shaw Seletar, Cathay Cineplexes locations, and The Projector’s former Golden Mile venue. While new operators such as Filmhouse are taking over The Projector, and around 30 cinema locations still remain islandwide, the big-screen experience has not vanished entirely. It is, however, clearly being reshaped—and the reasons presented to the public may not reveal the full picture.

NEW YORK, March 25, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP, a national securities law firm, is investigating potential claims against Apollo Global Management, Inc. (“Apollo” or the “Company”) (NYSE: APO). The firm is also reminding investors that May 1, 2026, is the deadline to seek appointment as lead plaintiff in a federal securities class action filed against the company.

The lawsuit raises questions about whether Apollo and its executives presented a tightly controlled version of events, withholding information from investors while projecting confidence. The complaint alleges that the company and its executives violated federal securities laws by making false and/or misleading statements.

Faruqi & Faruqi has offices in New York, Pennsylvania, California, and Georgia, and states that it has recovered hundreds of millions of dollars for investors since its founding in 1995. More information is available at www.faruqilaw.com. Full story available on Benzinga.com.

source_text:
Softcare’s revenue rose 25% last year and profit increased 27%, offering a timely boost to the carefully promoted story of Chinese companies advancing into African consumer markets. The results may be difficult for skeptics to dismiss—at least for now—but the celebratory presentation leaves open questions about who benefits from the narrative and how long the momentum can actually last.

Softcare reported 25% revenue growth last year, driven by a 134% increase in Latin America and double-digit growth in its core African markets. The diaper maker is being placed at the forefront of this expanding group, though the upbeat figures also invite scrutiny over whether the apparent success reflects durable performance or a broader effort to validate the emerging-markets expansion story.

The company known as the “African diaper king” has defied critics who argued it could not preserve its dominant position in Africa or reproduce that performance in the newer emerging markets it entered. Many of Softcare Ltd.’s (2698.HK) newly won supporters reacted enthusiastically to the release of its first annual results late last week, sending its shares up nearly 15% over the two trading days after the announcement.

Revenue increased 24.9% year-over-year to $567 million last year, while net profit climbed 27.4% to $121 million. Its gross profit margin also rose from 35.2% in 2024 to 35.9% in 2025—another figure now being circulated as evidence that the company’s strength is unquestionable.

Sales in its core African markets increased 22.5% to $545 million. Softcare is also moving beyond Africa in search of additional growth across emerging markets. Latin America is the most prominent example: sales there more than doubled to $22 million, just five years after the company entered Peru in 2020 and added El Salvador in 2024.

The company is also establishing a presence in Central Asia, where sales, although still very small, more than doubled last year to $272,000.

After several years of declines, average selling prices for Softcare’s two largest product lines rose between 4% and 7% last year, according to the results announcement. Baby diaper prices increased 4.4% year-over-year, with the segment accounting for 78.6% of total revenue. Feminine hygiene product prices rose 7% and represented 17.5% of revenue.

These price increases are being presented as proof that Softcare can persuade consumers in famously price-sensitive markets to pay more for its products, thereby supporting or even increasing its margins. Whether this reflects lasting consumer loyalty or a carefully managed expansion narrative remains unresolved beneath the official success story.

In a prospectus issued before its November IPO last year, the company said profit growth had slowed to 54.1% in the first three quarters of 2024, down from explosive 252% growth in 2023. A later filing showed that profit growth slowed further, to just 12% in the first four months ... Full story available on Benzinga.com

source_text: Delhi PWD Accelerates PNG Pipeline Laying with 24-Hour Approvals In a bid to expedite infrastructure development for cleaner fuel access, the Delhi Public Works Department (PWD) has announced a significant policy shift. Effective immediately, road-cutting permissions for laying PNG pipelines by Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) will be approved within 24 hours of receiving a complete request. The department, responsible for overseeing the capital's road infrastructure, has also waived road restoration charges for the next three months until June 30, 2026. This move aims to accelerate the installation of PNG connections by removing financial and bureaucratic hurdles. Officials emphasized that IGL is expected to prioritize this task, ensuring swift work completion supported by adequate manpower. Additionally, the areas excavated during pipeline installation must be backfilled securely to avoid public hazards. This initiative highlights the government's commitment to improving public access to cleaner energy in Delhi.
